index.title: The croc blog: guides, experiments, and release notes
index.description: Release notes, experiments, and practical guides to sending files with croc.
index.imageAlt: An open field notebook containing simple symbols for a relay, code tiles, a key, and a file.

posts.title: croc v11.5 can update itself
posts.seoTitle: croc v11.5: Safe Self-Updates and Clearer SSH Sessions
posts.description: croc v11.5 adds a verified standalone updater and clearer messages for shared SSH sessions.
posts.imageAlt: Three black-and-white panels show a version check, a verified standalone update, and a shared SSH terminal ending clearly in croc v11.5.

posts.title: croc v11.4 shares the terminal
posts.seoTitle: croc v11.4: Secure Terminal Sharing from CLI and Browser
posts.description: croc v11.4 shares one persistent terminal through separate read/write and read-only invitations, from the CLI or browser.
posts.imageAlt: Three black-and-white panels show native terminal hosting, browser joining, and separate read/write and read-only roles in croc v11.4.

posts.title: Share a terminal with croc ssh
posts.seoTitle: croc v11.4 SSH: Share a Terminal with a Six-Word Code
posts.description: Run croc ssh to share one terminal, with separate read/write and read-only invitations for CLI and browser guests.
posts.imageAlt: Three black-and-white panels show one host shell, a shared PTY, and separate read/write and read-only invitations.

posts.title: croc v11.3 goes peer-to-peer
posts.seoTitle: croc v11.3: Tailcat WireGuard, DERP, and Relay Fallback
posts.description: croc v11.3 adds direct WireGuard transfers, with public DERP and croc relays available when a direct route is blocked.
posts.imageAlt: Three black-and-white panels show Tailcat direct transport, public DERP fallback, and the established croc relay path.

posts.title: How fast is croc?
posts.seoTitle: croc Speed Test: Ten CLI File-Transfer Tools Compared
posts.description: I compared croc, SCP, rsync, and other file-transfer tools with a full Git clone and a 317.52 MB audio file from Mac to Toronto.
posts.imageAlt: Two terminal windows exchange an audio file across the United States while a stopwatch measures the transfer.

posts.title: From croc v10 to v11
posts.seoTitle: croc v11: Features and Fixes from v11.0.0 to v11.1.1
posts.description: croc v11 strengthens the handshake and relay limits, adds group stored transfers, and makes browser startup and terminal output clearer.
posts.imageAlt: Three black-and-white panels use a shield, group, and lightning icon to represent the croc v11 release.

posts.title: Why croc works this way
posts.description: Croc began with a turkey documentary I wanted to send to a friend, without asking her to configure a file-transfer system.
posts.imageAlt: Two computers connected by a direct line, with a shared key and confirmation checkmark.

posts.title: The relay is not a waiting room
posts.description: The relay forwards encrypted bytes as they arrive, so the receiver can start before the sender finishes.
posts.imageAlt: Two devices connected through a central relay, with three file packets moving between them.

posts.title: What the three words are doing
posts.description: Three words help croc clients meet and authenticate a fresh key. They still need to be kept private while the transfer is live.
posts.imageAlt: Blank code tiles converge into one cryptographic key.

posts.title: PAKE, step by step
posts.description: How croc turns a shared phrase into a fresh key, checks both peers, and keeps the phrase and key off the network.
posts.imageAlt: Two computers exchange messages and independently derive the same cryptographic key.

posts.title: Send a file without installing anything
posts.description: Choose files, share the code, and keep the browser open until the receiver has verified the transfer.
posts.imageAlt: A web browser sends a file directly to a receiving device.

posts.title: A browser and a terminal can share the same file
posts.description: The browser and CLI can join the same croc transfer, so each person can use the interface that suits their device.
posts.imageAlt: A browser window and command-line terminal are connected by a file transfer.

posts.title: When both computers cannot be online at once
posts.description: Stored mode lets the sender finish now and the receiver download later, within a chosen lifetime and download limit.
posts.imageAlt: A locked parcel waits for a limited time and a configured number of verified downloads.

posts.title: Send one file to a group, on their schedule
posts.description: Upload one encrypted file for a group, then choose how many downloads can finish and when the transfer expires.
posts.imageAlt: One locked parcel branches toward three recipient devices while a clock marks the shared download window.

posts.title: 40 ways to send a file
posts.seoTitle: 40 Ways to Send a File: croc and 39 Alternatives
posts.description: Forty file-transfer tools compared by resume support, accounts, browser and CLI access, encryption, availability, and transfer routes.
posts.imageAlt: File transfer tools comparison showing one file connected to browser, CLI, desktop, mobile, cloud, and synchronization routes.
